prompt: A photograph taken in 1991 of a small independent filling station on the edge of a farm town in east-central Illinois. A flat canopy on square steel posts over two islands of late-1980s fuel pumps with mechanical rolling number dials and small digital price displays. A small brick and painted-block station building with a service bay, its plate-glass window covered in advertisements: red and white Marlboro and Winston cigarette signs, a Coca-Cola sign in the 1991 red-and-white livery, hand-lettered price cards, an ICE chest and a stack of windscreen-wash outside the door. A 1989 Ford F-150 pickup with flush headlights at the near pump and a 1990 Chevrolet Lumina sedan at the far one. A payphone on the wall, a newspaper vending box, a rubbish bin, a rack of propane cylinders. Utility poles, flat cropland beginning immediately behind the lot. Late afternoon, clear sky. Shot on Kodak Gold 400 35mm colour negative and printed at a one-hour photo lab: crisp, neutral to slightly cool colour, good contrast, fine grain. IMPORTANT: this is 1991, not the 1970s. No sun-bleached vintage warm cast, no muted earth tones, no 1950s or 1970s Americana styling, no round-topped vintage petrol pumps, no boxy 1970s cars. Nothing later than 1991: no modern cars, no card readers, no LED signage.
